comments.body:
The complication is that WebAC uses the term "agent" for this:

https://github.com/solid/web-access-control-spec#describing-agents
Aaron Birkland:  okay - well that makes sense why "user agent" is used in the first place.  I'm content to close this one unless you or anyone feels that it should be addressed.

I think it's important to represent both the user and the software the user is using to interact with the repository.  And I agree that if we're using the term "userAgent" it should be the software, not the user themselves.

Andrew Woods The user agent concept is introduced in WebAC (https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-auth-webac/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/auth/webac/WebACRolesProvider.java#L101). And I think fedora-event-serialization/Modeshape use the user agent term (https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-event-serialization/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/event/serialization/JsonLDEventMessage.java#L193) as well. Do we want to change the environment variable fcrepo.auth.webac.userAgent.baseUri that is used across Fedora as well? It could be a breaking change for WebAC if we want to change it.

Danny Bernstein: I am trying to determine the intent of this ticket. Are you suggesting that the following method be changed to 'FedoraSession.getUserURI()'?

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/55acd4bd2c226968d933afe4ca75118311a2eb57/fcrepo-kernel-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/api/FedoraSession.java#L73
Andrew Woods: Yes. That's right.

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1247

I've rename it and also refactor the codes to use of a global constant for the related environment variable
fcrepo.auth.webac.userAgent.baseUri that are shared across WebAC and fedora-event-serialization as well.
Pending rebase and refactoring based on: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1243
Andrew Woods I've rebased it and renamed signature UserAgent to UserURI in FedoraEvent as suggested by Danny Bernstein in his review . See commit.

renderedFields.description:
In https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2608, the userAgent URI was introduced into the session. The HTTP user agent header definition is at odds with the way the term is being used here:

According the http spec the user-agent header is used for identifying the software agent acting on behalf of the user (https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec14.html#sec14.43). In FedoraSession we are using it to mean a URI representation of the user proper.

To prevent confusion I propose changing the member to "userURI".
